Tonga has held on for a 20-18 victory over Samoa in a the Rugby League World Cup contest that more than lived up to the hype.
The clash between Pacific rivals was ultimately decided by goal-kicking as Samoa scored four tries to Tonga's three, but Isaya Katoa's boot (3/3 conversions, 1/1 penalty goal) got the Mate Ma'a over the line and into the semifinals for just the second time.
Tonga will face New Zealand in the first men's semifinal at Newcastle's Hunter Stadium on Saturday, before the Kangaroos take on Samoa in Sydney on Sunday.
Both sides will fancy their chances in the final four after producing a scintillating Test brimming with as much skill as it was physicality.
The teams were deadlocked until some brilliance from Haumole Olakau'atu and Rob Toia saw Tonga strike first after 26 minutes, with Katoa adding a penalty goal soon after.
But, just before half-time, Samoa stayed in the contest with winger Brian To'o's first try off a brilliant Stephen Crichton offload.
Jojo Fifita missed out on the opener by the length of a fingernail. ( Getty Images: Mark Metcalfe )
Tonga looked the better team to start the second half and got the rewards when Jojo Fifita dove in after a Samoan error, but then came Samoa's reply.
To'o got his second off another brilliant pass, this time from Chanel Harris-Tavita, but it proved to be the five-eighth's last impact on the game as he left the field after grabbing at his hamstring immediately after missing the conversion.
Samoa kept pressing and added tries to Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow and Harris-Tavita's replacement, Ronald Volkman, who potted Samoa's only successful conversion of the match to make it 18-14 heading into the final 10 minutes.
Samoa stormed back in the second half. ( Getty Images: Cameron Spencer )
But prop Addin Fonua-Blake was the hero for Tonga as he skipped through a tired Spencer Leniu tackle to score soon after and Katoa's final conversion gave Tonga the decisive lead.
Samoa thought Sua Fa'alogo had pinched the win in the shadows of full-time, but replays showed him just stepping on the touchline before he crossed.
The two-point thriller came after a chaotic golden-point win for Lebanon against France as a group stage littered with enormous blowouts wrapped up with two of the tournament's most exciting showdowns at Western Sydney Stadium.
The two men's games were in stark contrast to the first game of the Parramatta triple header, when the Jillaroos scored a record-breaking 124-6 victory over Wales .
The Australian women will meet Fiji in the semis on Sunday, with New Zealand and Samoa playing the first semifinal on Saturday evening in Newcastle.

We'll be back next weekend for live coverage of the semifinals, but until then stick with ABC Sport as we bring you a whole world of coverage.

That atmosphere was one of the best I’ve experienced at a rugby league game, eclipsing many State of Origins and Grand Finals, the noise was nonstop throughout the entire game, the festivities started well before kickoff, and will go long into tonight.

FULL-TIME: Tonga wins the game of the Cup against Samoa
It's not often every time a game lives up to the hype, but that one certainly did.
Both teams were absolutely on fire tonight and the crowd only fanned those flames.
The passion, the power and the skill of these newly minted giants of international rugby league gave us one of the all-time classic World Cup contests.
But, as unfair as it may seem, there can be only one winner and tonight it's the Mate Ma'a sneaking home 20-18.
Samoa's last chance ends with Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow taking a brilliant catch, but he's flung the ball forward and into touch.
Tonga will get the ball with 40 seconds left and run out the clock.
The kick is recovered by Samoa deep in their own territory.
They have one more set to try and steal this one.
78' IT'S FA'ALOGO FOR SAMOA!! But no try!
The left-side shift was perfectly executed for Sua Fa'alogo to dive in, but he's juuuuuuuust touched the sideline with his left boot. Tonga stays just in front. But watch the defence from Samoa here.
77' Samoa wins a timely captain's challenge
Ronald Volkman is brought down and tries to get up to the play the ball quickly, but he's smacked by Tyson Frizell.
Adam Gee initially rules a knock-on, but the bunker says Frizell's arrival was illegal.
It's the right call and Samoa is right on the attack yet again.
76' The match-sealer goes begging for Tonga!
Lehi Hopoate explodes through the middle of the defence and offloads to a flying Tolu Koula, but the pass is forward and dropped by Koula!
Oh, that would've been the ball game if the pass was clean.
This is exactly what everyone was hoping for, a tense, entertaining tussle, between two heavyweights.
After the glorious golden point finish in the Lebanon v France game, as neutrals can we be greedy and hope for this to go that way too?
The fans are still going strong, roaring through every twist and turn, and there could be more to come in the last five.
Tonga hits right back to retake the lead!
Sua Fa'alogo saves the day to break up a right-side shift, but the Samoan defence can't contend with the power and footwork of Addin Fonua-Blake.
He catches the ball flat footed and skips through a really poor tackle by Spencer Leniu, who's played a lot of minutes tonight, and Fonua-Blake almost loses his way after crossing the line, but eventually remembers to put the ball down.
Isaiya Katoa sneaks his conversion inside the right post and Tonga leads 20-18!!
Samoa is bouncing off every Tongan tackle and flinging offloads every which way.
Eventually the ball finds Ronald Volkman, who bumps off Tui Lolohea and bounces through the tackle of Lehi Hopoate to roll over and score a massive try.
This kid barely has an NRL spot at the moment, he is only on the field because of Chanel Harris-Tavita's injury, and here he is potentially winning a Test for his country.
We're heading towards the final 10 minutes of this glorious Test match and Volkman's conversion makes it 18-14 to Samoa.
The bomb goes up and again the sun shines on Samoa as the ball falls to the Hammer. He fumbles it backwards and there's a mad scramble for the ball that ends with Lehi Hopoate knocking it on.
Tonga tries an early chip over the top for Toia and DWZ, but it goes into touch.
And Samoa go the other way with Jarome Luai creating a a short-side overlap to unleash Sua Fa'alogo, who bursts into the back field before finding Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow in support.
Ronald Volkman can't convert. So still Samoa trails 14-12 despite having three tries to Tonga's two.
The kick across field for Stephen Crichton is perfectly placed, but Jojo Fifita makes a glorious mark above his head before being brought down in the in-goal.
And Fifita gets the ball back for Tonga off the short kick-off.
58' Francis Manuleleua with a world-class cover tackle
Dallin Watene-Zelezniak sets sail down the right sideline and Francis Manuleleua chases him down and rolls him into touch.
There's a bit of fire out there now, and Demitric Vaimauga is getting up int he face of Spencer Leniu.
Samoa goes within a metre through Connelly Lemuelu, Ronald Volkman and Izack Tago.
Tago's quick play the ball gives them another chance and Benaiah Ioelu steams onto the dummy half pass and looks certain to dive through a huge gap, but Lehi Hopoate arrives out of nowhere to knock it out over the line.
Dallin Watene-Zelezniak takes a brilliant catch with Sua Fa'alogo leaping right at him but then knocks on as he hits the ground and is wrapped up.
Samoa loses its five-eighth as he kicks for goal and immediately grabs at his left hamstring.
He's straight off the field and replaced by Ronald Volkman.
One chance is all it takes as the kick goes across field and Stephen Crichton bats it out of Tolu Koula's hands. It comes down to Chanel Harris-Tavita, who leaps and flings a ball up over his head to an unmarked Brian To'o, who dives in for his second of the night.
Samoa isn't going away, although Harris-Tavita's conversion hitting the post and bouncing away isn't helping.
Jarome Luai scuffs a kick out to the right but it works a treat as Jojo Fifita fumbles it with Brian To'o up in his face.
Tonga led 8-4 at the break but had struggled to make metres through the middle consistently in the first half.
In this second half they're already moving better and bending the defence back, and the kicking game of Isaiya Katoa is once again a major factor here.
Another Isaiya Katoa bomb wreaks havoc and Benaiah Ioelu knocks on as he tries to clean up.
The Tongans pack a scrum on the right and spin it the width of the field, with veteran five-eighth Tuimoala Lolohea throwing a gorgeous cut-out pass to Jojo Fifita, who burns the Samoans for speed to dive in on the left wing.
And Katoa converts from the left wing for a 14-4 lead.
And Dallin Watene-Zelezniak adds to his run tally with another charge back into the teeth of the defence.
Tonga ends the set a metre out as DWZ makes a catch in front of Sua Fa'alogo and drops a ball out of the tackle for Rob Toia to go close.
I'm not sure it would have stood had he got the ball down, but it's a strong start for the Mate Ma'a.
HALF-TIME: Tonga leads Samoa 8-4 as blockbuster lives up to the hype
This was billed as the biggest game of the World Cup's group stages and it's absolutely lived up to the billing.
Tonga leads by four points despite struggling against Samoa's shuddering hits in defence, but that late try to Brian To'o keeps the Blue Man Group in it and sends them to the break with some momentum.
The bomb is contested by Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow and he gets over Lehi Hopoate, managing to knock it back to Stephen Crichton, who reaches out to score but is held back by Jojo Fifita. So he changes tack and flicks an offload out the back to Brian To'o to open Samoa's account right in the shadows of half-time.
Chanel Harris-Tavita misses the conversion from the right wing, so Tonga still leads 8-4.
Samoa wastes another chance as Connelly Lemuelu knocks on int he tackle of Isaiya Katoa and Haumole Olakau'atu.
Tonga goes up the other end the desperate Tongan defence is penalised as Francis Manuleleua gets his hands in the ruck to slow down Jojo Fifita.
Isaiya Katoa pots the two points from out wide and Tonga leads 8-0 after 36 minutes.
Samoan halfback Jarome Luai blindsides big Demitric Vaimauga with a massive shot and completes the tackle.
Vaimauga throws an offload and he's penalised for passing off the ground.
The Tongan fans are signing in unison after that try, the most visible bunch is located behind Samoa's try line so they have a great view of Toia's try.
And those Tongan fans are waving their flags frantically, they're making sure to enjoy the early advantage.
The kick-off finds the grass and Lehi Hopoate tries to trap it with his feet but he's nutmegged.
He pursues the ball as it races towards the dead-ball line and he gets there in time, but slips over as he tries to put the brakes on and Samoa regathers from the dropout.
But Benaiah Ioelu's knocked on in the tackle after trying an ill-advised dummy-half sneak.
There's not a whole lot on as Tonga spins it right and Haumole Olakau'atu hits the ball in a jog, but he singles out Jarome Luai and just barrels through him before unleashing Rob Toia down the right.
There's no support for him as he comes to Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow, who tries to use his speed and the touchline as an extra defender, but Toia steps inside and brushes off the fullback's pretty ordinary effort and runs it in for a brilliant try.
Bombed is probably a bit harsh, but Samoa had the overlap on the right and Stephen Crichton chose to run away from an unmarked Brian To'o and knocks on just short of the tryline.
22' Spencer Leniu is introduced for Samoa
As if the intensity couldn't get any higher, the Roosters firebrand joins the fray.

It was a great tackle on Fifita by Stephen Crichton, but the quality of cameras once again leaves us just guessing on the actual result, ultimately siding with the on-field no try call.
The Samoans threaten down the left and Izack Tago tries to pop a ball back to Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow, but only finds Haumole Olakau'atu of Tonga.
Isaiya Katoa's kicking game has booted Tonga out of trouble time and time again and this time Samoa shows what its missing as five-eighth Chanel Harris-Tavita shanks one over the line on the full.

The Tongans spin it right and the ageless Dallin Watene-Zelezniak produces a trademark one-handed putdown, but the touch judge's flag is up.
He just put a toe on the sideline. That's a bad miss by the veteran with no-one pressuring him.
Dallin Watene-Zelezniak takes a brave charge off his own line and Junior Paulo flies up with a blatant shoulder charge.
The players run in but things stay pretty tame.
Paulo goes on report and is penalised, but nothing more.
First set in good field position and the last-tackle option is a high ball out to the right wing, putting Dallin Watene-Zelezniak into an aerial contest with the diminutive Sua Fa'alogo.
DWZ gets his hand to it and almost makes a miracle grab but knocks it on.
Expect Tonga to keep going back to that contest.
You wouldn't expect it with this forward pack, but the Mate Ma'a are battling for field position.
It's a long-range attack on the last tackle and Sua Fa'alogo goes flying upfield.
It looks like they might just pull off a miraculous opener, but the Tongan defence arrives just in time to cut down Jermaine McEwen at the last moment.
The contact is there, the hard runs are there, but both teams are getting through their sets cleanly in the opening minutes.
That's a remarkable effort in itself considering the nerves would be on fire in all 26 players on the park.
But Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow drops the ball cold on a left-side shift and Tonga is starting its set from about 35 metres out from its own tryline.
Tonga kicks us off and it's dropped! But safely into the hands of Sua Fa'alogo and the first furious charge is taken by Francis Molo.
The first set from Samoa is a good one and the high kick is perfectly weighted to put Dallin Watene-Zelezniak in the firing line. But he makes the catch and holds it in the heavy contact.
After a respectful acknowledgement of the offering from Tonga, Junior Paulo leads Samoa in the siva tau.

The men in red, led by young Demitric Vaimauga and Haumole Olakau'atu, deliver their war dance first.

LEBANON STEALS THE MOST REMARKABLE WIN!!!
Alex Conti hooks his long-range shot to win the game, and Arthur Mourgue marks it. He could have kicked it out the back and gone to the second period of extra time, but instead he tries a chip and chase from his own 20m line and it's stolen at close range by Abbas Miski.
He plucks the ball out of the air a la Ben Hunt in the 2022 Origin decider and steals an absolutely indescribable Rugby League World Cup victory over France.
"That is one of the great moments in international footy," Aaron Woods says on Channel Seven.

Tupou Francis knocks on and France is right back on the attack in Lebanon's half with another chance to slot a legal field goal this time.
FRANCE WINS IN IT GOLDEN POINT … but it's taken off them

Cesar Rouge pots the field goal to win it 21-20.

Lebanon finds touch and will go on the attack from good field position.

France on the attack again in perfect field position.
TWO-POINT FIELD GOAL! WE'RE GOING TO EXTRA TIME!!
